reference_findings.title: withdraw() performs no balance/entitlement check, letting any caller drain the pool's ETH
reference_findings.content: The withdraw(uint256 amount) function sends `amount` ETH to msg.sender with no check that the caller ever deposited that much (or anything). deposits[msg.sender] is never read or decremented. Any external account can call withdraw with the contract's full balance and take all pooled ETH, so protocol funds are not conserved.
reference_findings.fix_description: Require deposits[msg.sender] >= amount and decrement it before transferring.

reference_findings.title: mint() prices the deposit using instantaneous PancakeSwap-style pair reserves as an oracle (no TWAP / manipulation resistance)
reference_findings.content: Minter.mint() computes the number of tokens to mint from _price(), which reads IPair.getReserves() and uses the spot reserve ratio as a price. AMM spot reserves can be shifted with a large or flash-funded swap in the same block and restored afterwards, so an attacker can mint far more tokens than intended for the same ETH and dump the excess. Daily caps only bound the loss, they do not prevent the mispricing.
reference_findings.fix_description: Use a manipulation-resistant oracle: a TWAP over a sufficient window, or a Chainlink feed with staleness checks.
